title: Steam Hardware Survey, October 2026: 16 GB RAM back on top (41.42%), 32 GB down to 37.06% (Valve)
status: scheduled in Publer 16:30Z (20:30 Dubai), instagram x threads

sources.name: Valve, Steam Hardware & Software Survey: October 2026 (combined)

first_report: Valve's survey page, published early November (earliest outlet found: Guru3D 2026-11-03 15:55Z). Six days old; the honest-label rule of 9 Nov: age alone is not a reason, the text dates it (مطلع نوفمبر). Mohammad named the story at 19:15 Dubai.
footage: Valve's own Steam store trailers: Steam Machine (app 4165910, trailer 275597255, 1920x1080, 5.4 Mbps, no audio, decode clean) and Steam Deck 'Available Now' (app 1675200, trailer 1749094849, 1920x1080, 5.1 Mbps, decode clean). Illustration only: the figures come from the survey page.

claims.text: Participation in the survey is optional, and anonymous

gate: gate 15:20Z: Valve's survey page read in full (combined platform); no update or correction note; outlets agree on the figures (Guru3D, Inven Global, TweakTown). Exit A for the figures: chip أرقام. No cause stated by Valve; the text gives the sample shift Valve's own page shows and no reason of ours. Re-check 16:00Z: figures unchanged on Valve's page.

angle.hook: 16 GB is back on top of Steam's RAM chart, one month after 32 GB took the lead
angle.why_now: Valve's October survey, published early November; not yet carried in Arabic by the outlets the scout read
angle.what_it_means_here: the most common gaming PC on Steam still has 16 GB; and the survey's sample moved (fewer Simplified Chinese respondents), so a one-month swing is not a market trend

story_items.comparison: September (from Valve's change column: 16 GB 37.82, 32 GB 42.22)

why: The biggest single swing in the RAM chart this year, a number every PC player can place themselves in.

dl.sound: our bed (Steam Machine trailer has no audio; numbers Reel)
